pr_title: Fix store/load float LCL_FIELD with unaligned offsets on arm32.
pr_body:
Use lea to instantiate LCL_VAR address in a register.

Also, after the change we have better code size for the test, before lclmorph regression change:
```
IN0003: 000024  4B      addw    r3, sp, 0x828	// [V00 loc0]
IN0004: 000028  2B      adds    r3, r3, 1
```
now:
```
IN0003: 000024  4B      addw    r3, sp, 0x829
```

Commits:
feb321aafeb: Add an additional test for the issue.
cecd8e466bc: Reenable the test.
b91991bae2d: Fix arm32 access to unaligned float fields.

Fixes #34170.
pr_comments:
> Although, looking at the ARMv7-M Architecture Reference Manual it seems that the offset need only be a multiple of 4 for both the double and single case; I'm not sure that makes enough difference to optimize for the double case.

Thanks, there are a few things that could be improved, but this one looks pretty safe to do in this PR. Added a commit that does that.
The newly added test failed on arm32 Linux and it does not fail on my arm32 windows, will have to investigate it further.
Merged, thanks @echesakovMSFT and @CarolEidt for the help with debugging and reviews.

issue_context.title: Assertion failed 'offsetFitsInVectorMem(emitGetInsSC(id))'
issue_context.body:
Windows arm32 with:
```
set COMPlus_TieredCompilation=0
set COMPlus_JitStress=1
```

From attempt to re-enable "runtime-coreclr jitstress" testing:
https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/public/_build/results?buildId=574937&view=results

```
    JIT\Methodical\explicit\coverage\expl_float_1_d\expl_float_1_d.cmd [FAIL]
      
      Assert failure(PID 7700 [0x00001e14], Thread: 10360 [0x2878]): Assertion failed 'offsetFitsInVectorMem(emitGetInsSC(id))' in 'TestApp:Main():int' during 'Generate code' (IL size 4230)
      
          File: F:\workspace\_work\1\s\src\coreclr\src\jit\emitarm.cpp Line: 465
          Image: D:\h\w\B77C09AB\p\CoreRun.exe
```

Tests:
```
JIT\Methodical\explicit\coverage\expl_float_1_d\expl_float_1_d.cmd
JIT\Methodical\explicit\coverage\expl_float_1_r\expl_float_1_r.cmd
```


category:correctness
theme:alignment
skill-level:intermediate
cost:medium
comments: @sandreenko Might any of your recent struct work have affected this?
This does not seem to need jit stress

My guess is this is due to `MorphLocalIndir` introduced in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/991. For arm32, if a field is a float/double at a not-aligned address, we should leave it to be processed by fgMorphField which will treat it as an IND, and the arm32 codegen knows how to deal with unaligned IND (see `emitInsLoadStoreOp`). Or, perhaps we need to teach the emitter about unaligned floating point field loads/stores using similar logic to `emitInsLoadStoreOp`.
As @jashook pointed out in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/34178, we should understand why this didn't fail in Linux arm runs. Was the test run there?

Looks like this is also failing in the rolling "runtime-coreclr outerloop" Windows arm test run job, starting after Windows arm testing was re-enabled with https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/32819

e.g., https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/public/_build/results?buildId=567481&view=logs&j=08fa9cb9-5528-5234-de15-5bfafb946da9&t=8fff87e1-0d46-5658-1051-6234077c6b03
@sandreenko Since this failure is affecting the regular outerloop job, I'm inclined to immediately disable the failing test for Windows arm32, since I don't think we have an easy fix here.
Have a pr out to do that

We do not run this test outside Windows:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/14a2f7897c744357566e678e59b3e725b50e5a52/src/coreclr/tests/src/JIT/Methodical/explicit/coverage/expl_float_1_r.csproj#L7

Note: We have ~300 tests with that condition, probably we should check them and see if it is still applicable.
I agree that we should double-check those tests. It's not helpful that there is no comment as to _why_ it is unsupported.
For a long time we did not support explicit layout on unix
Do you know why? Or if that's still true?

I opened https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/34250 to re-enable the explicit layout tests. Some are failing on Linux arm due to unaligned access. On Windows, unaligned accesses are fixed up by the OS.
@dotnet/jit-contrib the previous comment is the question that I mention at the meeting.

review_comments: that field store was represented as `IND float(ADD byref(LCL_VAR byref this, CNT_INT 1))` and we did not catch it in morph, so it was another issue, that was failing before `LCL_FLD` changes. I made a fix in morph to catch this pattern as well.
This access was failing before the PR that introduced #34990 because morph was generating `LCL_FLD` for it.
